rich_summary: Draupadi recounts to Bhima the humiliation inflicted by Kichaka, who assaulted and kicked her publicly while King Virata and others failed to intervene. She fears continued harassment and declares she would rather die than submit to him, urging Bhima to avenge the insult. Bhima promises vengeance but insists it must be done secretly to preserve the Pandavas’ disguise during their exile. Draupadi tricks the lustful Kichaka into agreeing to a secret nighttime meeting in the deserted dancing hall. Believing he is going to a tryst, Kichaka arrives adorned for love, only to encounter Bhima lying in wait. A brutal hand‑to‑hand struggle follows, shaking the hall, until Bhima overpowers and crushes him, killing the tyrant who had tormented Draupadi.

highlight_spans.why: Draupadi recounts the public humiliation when Kichaka kicked her before the court, establishing the emotional and moral stakes.
Draupadi demands vengeance from Bhima and threatens to take poison if Kichaka lives, a pivotal turning point that triggers the plot.
The deceptive arrangement of the secret meeting in the dancing hall shows Draupadi’s strategic intelligence and sets the trap.
The violent wrestling match between Bhima and Kichaka, described through animal and elemental imagery, forms the dramatic climax.

top_scenes.scene_text: In the dark deserted dancing hall, Bhima waits on a wooden bed in disguise while the ornamented Kichaka enters expecting a secret tryst.
Bhima and Kichaka grapple like enraged beasts at midnight, their colossal bodies crashing and shaking the pillars of the hall.
Draupadi, weeping with her face hidden in Bhima’s chest, begs him to avenge the humiliation she suffered in the royal court.
